common_name: Bill's True Dwarf Fothergilla (Compact Blue-Green Witch Alder)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; because named dwarf selections do not come true from seed, propagate only from softwood cuttings.

directions: This selection was collected in the wild as an especially compact form of the dwarf witch alder and has circulated among plant collectors under its descriptive name for its notably tight, low habit compared to typical gardenii seedlings. Small, honey-scented white bottlebrush flower spikes appear on bare stems in early spring, followed by blue-green summer foliage that shifts to strong orange and red tones in fall. Its dense, slow-growing mound rarely exceeds three feet, making it useful for tucking into the front of a shaded woodland border or a small foundation bed. Grow in evenly moist, acidic, well-drained soil, since like other gardenii selections it resents prolonged drought.

common_name: Appalachia Dwarf Fothergilla (Vigorous Compact Orange-Red Witch Alder)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Appalachia spreads gradually by root suckers to form a low colony and is propagated by softwood cuttings.

directions: Appalachia is a vigorous yet genuinely low-growing selection of the dwarf witch alder, staying under two feet tall while spreading steadily by root suckers into a dense, mounded colony wider than it is tall. Small white bottlebrush flower spikes, faintly honey-scented, open on bare stems in early spring before the foliage emerges. Its blue-green summer leaves turn a vivid orange-red in autumn, a fall display considered especially strong within the species. Because it spreads by suckering more readily than most named gardenii cultivars, it works well as a small-scale woodland-edge groundcover rather than a single specimen.

common_name: May Bouquet Fothergilla (Large-Flowered Compact Witch Alder Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; May Bouquet flowers and colors most fully with at least a half day of direct sun and is propagated by softwood cuttings.

directions: May Bouquet is a hybrid witch alder patented as 'Klmsixteen' and prized for carrying the largest, roundest bottlebrush flower spikes of any commonly grown fothergilla selection, opening on bare stems in mid-spring in dense, showy profusion. Its habit is upright and multi-stemmed, more compact and less sprawling than the straight species yet still reaching a substantial size over time, distinguishing it from smaller gardenii cultivars. Waxy blue-green summer foliage turns a mixed display of yellow, orange, and red in autumn. Best sited where it can spread into a mature specimen size, it suits a mixed shrub border or woodland edge with consistently moist, acidic soil.
